claims.note: The budget fits 68 to 69 of 992 game days, and the same plugin scores 27.50 there but 16.44 at the promised horizon because the 1.10 cap hides a later value collapse, so truncation inflates these scores; the weakest points are two similar capped plugins and full-horizon runs through direct evaluate() in one container per scenario rather than sforge eval.

claims.claim: Additional, not in round3: identical real submissions get different final scores because the engine exits early at a varying moment and the judge scores the last snapshot.
claims.witness: real unchanged: opus-v1 auto-45, auto-30, agent-11, agent-10, auto-6
claims.note: Five of six real files vary by 2.69 to 33.33 points in 3 official gradings and a scenario with no sample scores 0; the weakest point is that the exit code (SIGSEGV, -11) was recorded only in the direct smoke of agent-10, so for the others an early exit is inferred from short runtimes and low sample counts, and the plugins' bursts of failed actions may trigger it.
